note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: KV-Latent: dimension-level KV cache reduction via down-sampling, two-stage training, frequency-aware RoPE, and results

nodes.name: KV cache is an efficiency bottleneck
nodes.description: The KV cache grows linearly with generated tokens, and its large volume and per-request dedicated storage cause memory consumption and bandwidth bottlenecks in LLM decoding.

nodes.name: K,V are low-rank down-sampling transforms
nodes.description: In MHA, K and V down-sample the d-dimensional hidden state into d_h-dimensional vectors (Q^T and O up-sample), so the KV cache stores low-rank latents and need not keep full-dimension vectors; directly reducing K/V head size is under-explored.

nodes.name: Head dim can be decoupled
nodes.description: Within a head, the K-Q^T pair and V-O pair need not share dimension: d_h can be split into d_qk and d_vo, decoupling n_h*d_h=d and d_h=d_qk=d_vo.

nodes.name: Down-sample pretrained weights then retrain
nodes.description: KV-Latent reduces KV cache by directly down-sampling pretrained W_K and W_V (and W_Q, W_O) to smaller head dimension with a RoPE-compatible channel selection, then restores performance with LoRA on FFNs and two-stage training.

nodes.name: Two-stage training recovers performance
nodes.description: Stage I is in-layer distillation keeping hidden states consistent between original and reduced layers; Stage II is end-to-end training (next-token prediction or KL distillation), using less than 1% of pretraining tokens.

nodes.name: RoPE is unstable at low dimension
nodes.description: RoPE shows significant numerical instability on low-dimensional vectors: when dimension d < 32 the oscillation range is comparable to the intended attenuation, losing positional encoding ability.

nodes.name: High-frequency channels cause the noise
nodes.description: Low-numbered (high-frequency) channels contribute most of the RoPE noise, while high-numbered (low-frequency) channels remain relatively stable though decaying more slowly.

nodes.name: Frequency-aware RoPE sampling
nodes.description: Densifying sampling of low-frequency rotations and avoiding high-frequency rotations (Formula 11) improves RoPE stability at low dimension and reduces negative values while preserving attenuation.

nodes.name: KV-Latent retains performance with smaller cache
nodes.description: KV-Latent on LLaMA-2 and LLaMA-3-8B retains satisfactory MMLU, OBQA, ARC and needle-in-haystack performance while reducing KV cache size (e.g. 50% and 75% reductions), improving efficiency.

nodes.name: Limits of recovery
nodes.description: Limited training volume prevents full recovery of model proficiency, and at d_qk = d_vo = 16 performance failed to recover, suggesting a lower bound on KV cache size.

nodes.name: GQA-trained models are harder to compress
nodes.description: LLaMA-2 (no GQA) outperforms LLaMA-3 relative to its baseline when trained on fewer tokens, indicating models already using GQA are harder to adapt with KV-Latent.

nodes.name: Values carry more information than keys
nodes.description: Allocating more dimension to d_vo than d_qk consistently yields better efficiency and effectiveness, suggesting keys carry less essential information than values and are more compressible.

nodes.name: Orthogonal to other KV reduction methods
nodes.description: KV-Latent works with head-level (LLaMA-3 GQA), layer-level and token-level methods, e.g. combined with PyramidInfer at 50% compression, and is orthogonal to mainstream methods.

isolated_nodes.name: LoRA rank has little effect on log PPL
isolated_nodes.description: Increasing LoRA rank increases training time while log PPL changes only slightly (Table 3), though the effect may be larger at larger scale.

isolated_nodes.name: Smaller cache is faster
isolated_nodes.description: KV cache efficiency aligns with its size: the smaller the overall volume, the faster both pre-filling and generation speeds, and the larger the maximum supported cache n_max.

structural_reasoning: Cache bottleneck and the low-rank view motivate down-sampling with two-stage training; RoPE instability analysis yields the frequency-aware fix; both feed the main results, from which limits, compatibility and parameter-choice findings follow.
